hypothesis.title: The Adaptation Boundary
hypothesis.question: What makes a musical transformation preserve identity rather than destroy it?
hypothesis.hypothesis: Musical transformations remain intelligible when adaptation is assigned to the layer or axis that can change while a separate identity-bearing layer remains invariant. If adaptation happens at the wrong boundary, context and labels cannot recover what the representation has already erased.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: Supported by recent extractions on speech-enhancement layer asymmetry, representational geometry under perturbation, factor-partitioned speech embeddings, dysarthric ASR context failures, and vowel-distance alignment for dubbing. Together they suggest that musical variation is best treated as controlled adaptation: preserve identity in one layer while allowing repair or expressive change in another.

recipe.title: Adaptation Boundary Study
recipe.bodyMd: Create a one-minute phrase study. Keep phrase length constant while making five versions: stable core/adaptive surface, geometric perturbation, axis-separated variation, late-label failure, and vowel-aligned translation. Listen for which identity survives: phrase, speaker, instrument, groove, harmony, emotion, or mouth-shape.
dawChecklist: Choose one short source phrase with strong identity
Vary only one adaptation boundary per pass
Document which perceptual identity survives each pass

protocol.listeningMethod: A/B compare each transformed pass against the source and write the surviving identity cues
